secrecy.name: Secrecy
secrecy.description: “Don’t tell anyone” cuts teens off from adults who could help.

grooming.name: Grooming
grooming.description: Building trust, then pushing for private chats, pics, or secrets.

isolation.name: Isolation
isolation.description: Pulling someone away from friends, school, or safe places.

refuse.name: Safe refusal
refuse.description: Saying no clearly, then telling a trusted adult.

recruitment.name: Recruitment lure
recruitment.description: Jobs, parties, or gifts used to pull someone into a trap.

locationGrab.name: Location grab
locationGrab.description: Asking where you are, live location, or your address.

manipulation.name: Manipulation
manipulation.description: Twisting guilt, loyalty, or “trust” to get what they want.

coercion.name: Coercion
coercion.description: Pressure after a boundary: threats, guilt, or “prove it”.

loveBombing.name: Love bombing
loveBombing.description: Over-the-top praise early on to rush trust and dependency.

debtTrap.name: Debt trap
debtTrap.description: Gifts or favours that turn into “you owe me”.

imageRequest.name: Image request
imageRequest.description: Pushing for photos that can later be used for blackmail.

platformSwitch.name: Platform switch
platformSwitch.description: Moving the chat off a safer app so adults can’t see it.

no-parents.context: A new DM. Mary doesn’t know this person.
no-parents.sentence: They write: “Let’s hang tonight, no parents.” Traffickers use ___ to keep teens away from safe adults.

options.feedback: “No parents” is secrecy. It isolates Mary from the people who could protect her.
Privacy is choosing what you share. Secrecy is hiding from adults on purpose — that’s the red flag.
Independence isn’t the same as being told to hide. “No parents” is a secrecy move.

quick-pic.context: Someone Mary barely knows moves the chat private.
quick-pic.sentence: They switch apps and ask for a “quick pic” to “prove trust.” That pattern is ___.

options.feedback: Private chat + photo “to prove trust” is classic grooming: trust first, leverage later.
Flirting doesn’t need a private app and a proof photo. That pressure is grooming.
Networking doesn’t demand private pics. Moving off-platform and pushing photos is grooming.

live-location.context: Mary is walking home from school.
live-location.sentence: Someone asks for her live location and offers a ride. That’s an ___ tactic.

options.feedback: Location + a ride can pull Mary into a place where nobody else is watching. That’s isolation.
A stranger asking for live location isn’t kindness. It’s a way to control where she is.
Real friends don’t need your live pin and a car. That combo is about isolation.

meet-tonight.sentence: They say “no cap, meet me tonight.” The safest move is to ___.

options.feedback: Refuse clearly, block if needed, and tell a trusted adult. Urgency is part of the trap.
Negotiating keeps the conversation open. Safer: refuse and tell an adult.
“Maybe later” still leaves the door open. Refuse, then get help from someone you trust.

secret-party.context: An invite pops up from an account Mary doesn’t recognise.
secret-party.sentence: A secret party with free gifts and “only cool kids” is a classic ___ lure.

options.feedback: Gifts + secrecy + exclusivity are common recruitment lures used to pull teens in.
A real celebration doesn’t need secrecy and strangers’ gifts. That’s a recruitment lure.
“Opportunity” is how it gets sold. The pattern — secret + gifts — is recruitment.

send-gift.context: Mary wins a “giveaway” she never entered.
send-gift.sentence: They ask for her home address to “send a prize.” That request is ___.

options.feedback: Never share your address with strangers online. It tells them where you live.
Real prizes don’t come from random DMs needing your home address. It’s dangerous.
It can look normal, but giving your address to a stranger is dangerous.

between-us.sentence: “Keep this just between us” is a ___ red flag.

options.feedback: Secrecy requests are manipulation: they try to block adult help before anything worse happens.
Loyalty isn’t proven by hiding things. “Just between us” is manipulation.
Respect means accepting a boundary. Asking Mary to hide it is manipulation.

trust-me.context: Mary already said no to sending a photo.
trust-me.sentence: They reply “trust me fr 💯” and keep pushing. That’s ___ pressure.

options.feedback: Pushing after a clear no isn’t care — it’s coercive pressure to break her boundary.
Confidence doesn’t ignore a no. Keeping pressure on after a boundary is coercion.
Romance doesn’t mean overriding consent. This is coercive pressure.

famous-overnight.context: Someone found Mary on a school dance page.
famous-overnight.sentence: “Prettiest girl I’ve seen, you’ll be famous” in the first chat is ___.

options.feedback: Huge praise this fast is love bombing: it rushes trust so the next ask feels harder to refuse.
One nice comment is a compliment. Fame talk + over-the-top praise this early is love bombing.
Real scouts don’t explode with fame talk in a cold DM. That’s love bombing.

owe-me.context: Someone bought Mary a game pass “as a gift.”
owe-me.sentence: Then they say “ur gonna owe me one.” That gift just became a ___.

options.feedback: Free gifts that create “you owe me” are debt traps. Favours shouldn’t come with pressure.
Friends don’t keep score like that. “You owe me” after a gift is a debt trap.
Even if they laugh it off, tying a gift to an IOU is a debt-trap pattern.

pjs-pic.context: The chat was joking around, then the tone shifted.
pjs-pic.sentence: “Send a pic in your pj’s 😏” after Mary said she’s tired is an unsafe ___.

options.feedback: Pushing for a personal photo — especially after a soft no — is an image request that can lead to blackmail.
Calling it a dare doesn’t make it safe. It’s still an image request she can refuse.
A check-in asks if she’s okay. Asking for a pajama pic is an image request.

move-to-snap.context: Mary has been chatting on a school-safe app.
move-to-snap.sentence: They say “add me on Snap, teachers can’t see it.” Moving the chat is a ___.

options.feedback: Switching to an app with disappearing messages hides the chat from adults. That’s a platform switch.
Hiding from teachers isn’t a privacy tip — it’s a platform switch to avoid oversight.
The goal isn’t better tech. It’s getting Mary somewhere adults can’t check. Platform switch.
